small_guidance:
- The current v3 kernel uses atomic_add across spatial tiles which serializes writes; switch to a single program per (N, OC) that loops over spatial tiles internally and accumulates a scalar sum in registers, eliminating atomics and the separate finalize kernel.
- Swap the loop order so IC is the inner GEMM-K dim with BLOCK_IC=64 (full IC=64) and use tl.dot on a [BLOCK_OHW, BLOCK_IC] x [BLOCK_IC, 1] reduction; add autotune configs with BLOCK_OHW in {128,256,512}, num_warps in {4,8}, num_stages in {2,3,4}.
- Hoist the kh/kw index math: precompute valid masks and ih/iw once per (kh,kw) outside the IC loop, and fold the bias+multiplier+1/OHW epilogue directly at the end of the same kernel (skip the finalize pass).
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as a gather-style implicit-GEMM where each program owns one (n, oc) pair and directly accumulates the scalar mean: loop over output spatial tiles, and inside each tile loop over (kh,kw) and use tl.dot over IC to compute the partial sum, then reduce across the tile into a single accumulator. Output is just N*OC scalars — no intermediate (N,OC,OH,OW) tensor, no atomics, no second kernel.
- Equivalently, exploit that mean over OH*OW commutes with the conv-transpose sum: still iterate the full output grid (preserve asymptotic FLOPs), but accumulate one scalar per (n,oc) so memory traffic for the output collapses from N*OC*OH*OW to N*OC. Grid = (N*OC,), each block persistent across all spatial tiles.
- Use channels-last input layout (N, IH, IW, IC) so the IC reduction dim is contiguous, enabling vectorized loads and tl.dot; fuse bias add, *multiplier, and /(OH*OW) into the final store. Consider tiling OC as well (BLOCK_OC=8-16) so one program amortizes the x loads across multiple output channels sharing the same input window.
